mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% over two months, it signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in the same period
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
